CrowdStrike just launched something every enterprise deploying AI agents needs to pay attention to: an AI Kill Switch.

It is a production-grade mechanism to halt autonomous AI agents in enterprise environments. And it arrived the same week Adobe and Smartsheet shipped agents directly inside their existing products.

The convergence is telling. AI agents are no longer pilot projects or innovation lab experiments. They are being embedded into the software your teams use daily. And the security industry is now racing to build the governance layer to match.

The adoption data makes the urgency clear. AI agent mentions in tech job postings have reached 14.8%, surpassing LLM mentions at 10.7%. The Model Context Protocol — an emerging standard for how agents communicate — jumped from 0.3% to 4.5% in just one year.

For business leaders, the question is straightforward: do you know what your AI agents can access? What actions they can take without human approval? And if something goes wrong at 2 AM, who can shut them down and how fast?

Most organizations cannot answer all three questions today. CrowdStrike is betting that gap is about to become the most urgent problem in enterprise security.
